description: q-Collatz nontrivial-cycle census: exhaustive parity-word enumeration over the Skein-Collatz map on Z[q^{±1}], testing the affine cycle candidate P0 = n_k/([2]_q^k - [3]_q^{k_odd}) for Skein-integrality (exact Laurent division) + parity self-consistency + return. Exploratory research probe (NOT canonical production).
method: exact integer Laurent-polynomial arithmetic; cycle equation ([2]_q^k - [3]_q^{k_odd}) P0 = n_k cleared to Z[q^±1]; integrality via exact Laurent division; primitive words only (imprimitive repetitions skipped).
findings: Through period 18, the ONLY integral self-consistent Skein-Collatz cycles are the positive 2-cycle {q^{-1}, 1+q^{-1}} and the negative fixed point {-q^{-2}}.
These are the exact q-lifts of the classical Collatz cycles: {1,2} (positive) and the negative fixed point {-1}. At q=1, q^{-1}->1, 1+q^{-1}->2, -q^{-2}->-1.
No nontrivial positive q-cycle exists up to period 18 — negative evidence for the nontrivial-cycle-exclusion half of the no-cycles claim, consistent with (but not proving) the conjecture.

The unknot polynomial 1 is NOT in the domain of C_q: 1(q=-1)=1 is neither 0 (q-even) nor -1 (q-odd). The genuine positive attractor is the 2-cycle {q^{-1}, 1+q^{-1}}, not the literal element 1. The conjecture's 'reaches 1' is a classical-limit shorthand.
scope: This is a bounded computational census (period <= 18), NOT a proof of nontrivial-cycle exclusion. It does not close the affine cycle problem (see docs/audits/2026-07-18-collatz-no-cycles-multiplicative-shadow-gap.md).

provenance.runtime: ~2 min single-core for period<=18; exact arithmetic, deterministic (no RNG).
